verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
verse.line: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
verse.translation: One should not give up the work suited to one's nature, Kaunteya, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by faults, as fire is by smoke.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'never change jobs'. It answers perfectionism, not a reason to stay where you're harmed.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, telling him not to abandon the work that fits his nature just because it is imperfect. Every undertaking has its flaws, Krishna says, just as fire has smoke. The point is that you could do the work that belongs to you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.for_you: You quit your job last week to build a brand, and you feel more alive than ever. That fire is yours, and it does not need to be perfect to be true. Keep showing up for the work that fits you.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: पुरुषार्थात्फलप्राप्तिर्देशकालवशादिह । प्राप्ता चिरेण शीघ्रं वा यासौ दैवमिति स्मृता ॥
verse.line: Effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That timing is what we call fate.
verse.translation: Results come from effort, sooner or later, depending on place and time. That arrival of the fruit, early or late, is what people call fate.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha tells Rama that effort, not some outside force, is what shapes a life. What people call fate is simply the result of past effort arriving on its own schedule. Today's effort is what builds tomorrow. You cannot control when the fruit comes, but you can control the planting and watering. The verse asks you to stop worrying about what is beyond your hands and to trust the work itself.
verse.for_you: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi tells Yudhishthira that waiting for fate to deliver is a mistake. Every attempt can end in success or failure, but not acting guarantees nothing. She argues that you could act because effort is the only honest response to the unknown. The verse asks you to do what is right for its own sake and then to work as if everything depends on your own hands.
verse.for_you: You are building your own brand and the result is not yet clear. You do not know if it will succeed or fail. That uncertainty is the price of starting. Do the work today because it is yours to do, not because you know it will pay off.

verse.speaker: Lakshman
verse.setting: At Lake Pampa, Lakshman pulls Ram out of despair after Sita has been taken.
verse.sanskrit: उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात् परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किंचिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
verse.line: There is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the one who has it, nothing is out of reach.
verse.translation: Noble brother, enthusiasm is powerful; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the person who has it, nothing in the world is out of reach.
verse.why: Beauty can sharpen grief; a friend can remind you of your own strength.

prasang.title: Grief in springtime at Pampa
prasang.summary: At the beautiful lake of Pampa in spring, everything reminds Ram of Sita and his grief deepens. Lakshman tells him there is no strength greater than enthusiasm, and to rouse himself.
prasang.story_hook: Spring had come to the lake, and every flower made Ram's grief worse.
prasang.lesson: Beauty can sharpen grief; a friend can remind you of your own strength.

verse.meaning: At Lake Pampa, Ram is grieving Sita's absence, and the beauty around him only deepens his sorrow. Lakshman sees him falter and reminds him that enthusiasm is the one force that can move mountains. He says that for someone who carries this fire, nothing in the world is impossible.
verse.for_you: You feel more alive than ever right now, but the hard days will test that feeling. When you wonder if you can keep going, find a friend who will remind you of your own strength. Let their words pull you back to the fire you started.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna to focus entirely on the work itself, without clinging to the outcome. The right belongs only to the action, not to its fruits. This means you could do the work fully, but not let the result own you. Care, plan, and aim, but let go of the need to control what happens next.
verse.for_you: write one post or send one pitch. Do that work completely, and then let it go. The result will come, but your energy today belongs to the doing, not the waiting.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verse.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
verse.line: So keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. That's how you rise.
verse.translation: Therefore, always do the work that has to be done, without attachment; by working without attachment a person reaches the highest.
verse.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

prasang.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on a battlefield, reminding him that even those who have found peace and have nothing left to gain still act. He says that the wise work for the sake of the world because others watch and follow their example. So do your work well and without holding on to the outcome. That is how you rise.
verse.for_you: You quit your job to build your brand. The fire is real. Today, do one small task that moves the work forward. Let it be enough. The work itself is the example.

story.title: Building the bridge
story.story_hook: The army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey said he knew how to build a bridge.
story.summary: Ram waits three days for the ocean to let him pass, then loses patience. The ocean reveals that Nala can build a bridge; Nala admits his skill and the whole army hauls trees and rocks for five days until the bridge reaches Lanka.
story.lesson: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

script: You quit your job last week and you feel more alive than ever. You are building a brand and nothing else matters right now. That fire is yours. You are afraid it will go out when the hard days arrive.
Arjuna is on the battlefield. He is terrified to fight. He tells Krishna he cannot take up the sword. And Krishna replied:
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत्, सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः.
In plain words: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.

Krishna says every undertaking has flaws. He compares them to smoke rising from a fire. The work suited to your nature has its faults. But they are part of the process. You do not abandon the path because it is imperfect. You offer the work back to something larger than yourself. This is harder than it sounds. It is easy to chase perfection. It is harder to stay with the path that is messy and yours.
You are building something of your own. Today, notice the flaws in your work. Do not let them stop you. They are the smoke of a fire that is burning bright. Keep showing up.
Your work is true even with its flaws.

depth.life: You quit your job last week and are building a brand. You feel more alive than ever. You are afraid of losing that fire when the hard days arrive.
depth.points: The work that fits you will always have flaws. Fire always has smoke. The smoke does not mean the fire is wrong. It means the fire is burning.
depth.practice: Name one small flaw in your brand today. Then do one task anyway.
depth.question: What is the smoke you are seeing in your fire right now?
